summary_paragraph: A male patient with Factor V Leiden and a history of aortic thrombus was readmitted with pleuritic chest pain and stable hemoptysis. Imaging confirmed the aortic clot was unchanged, with no new pulmonary embolism or DVT. He underwent bronchoscopy, which showed tracheobronchomalacia but no active bleeding. A post-procedural fever resolved without infection. Chronic pain and anxiety were addressed with medication adjustments, including increased gabapentin and tizanidine, and initiation of venlafaxine. Anticoagulation with Lovenox was continued given high clotting risk. The vascular and hematology teams recommended monitoring over surgery. He was discharged home with new medications including simvastatin, aspirin, and a clonazepam taper, with follow-up planned in multiple specialties and emphasis on primary care coordination.
problems: Embolism and thrombosis of thoracic aorta
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
